Team / Jordan —

Thanks for sending the redline on the Order Form (attached). I reviewed the indemnity section and we have three items that need quick alignment before legal can sign off and we can move to DocuSign:

1) Evidence custodian / liaison: Acme has added a clause that routes evidence requests through their procurement inbox; Kimberly and I discussed mapping specific internal liaisons so we have an ops owner to respond within the required SLA.
2) Defense vs. reimburse split: the redline tightens who controls defense. We need to confirm whether Acme expects Redwood to "control defense" for third‑party IP claims or prefers a hybrid where Redwood defends but Acme reimburses certain costs.
3) Insurance and offsets: procurement asked about insurance offsets and whether the indemnity obligation should be reduced by available insurance proceeds — that needs a short note in the Order Form.

Proposed next steps (quick):
- Kimberly: confirm the legal position we should push back with (short statement we can insert into the redline).
- Ben: propose the operations contact(s) who will act as evidence liaison for Redwood (name + email).
- Jordan / Acme procurement: confirm who on your side will be the evidence custodian and if you have a preferred SLA for initial acknowledgement (24 hrs / 48 hrs).

I've attached our redline suggestions to the Order Form and an internal evidence checklist for Ben to edit. If convenient, let's do a 30‑minute sync tomorrow to finalize language that legal can accept.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_v2_redline.pdf (redlines inline), evidence_checklist.xlsx (ops checklist)

Thanks —

On Mon, Jun 8, 2026 at 9:14 AM Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / Jordan —
>
> Thanks for sending the redline on the Order Form (attached). I reviewed the indemnity section and we have three items...

Couple quick points from legal:

- Defense control: Our standard is to "retain the right to assume sole control of the defense with counsel of its choice" for third‑party IP claims, with the customer having the right to participate at their own expense. We can accept a hybrid only if the customer (Acme) commits in writing to cooperate and to not settle without Redwood's consent — propose a one‑sentence insertion: "Customer shall not settle any claim that admits fault or obligates Redwood without Redwood's prior written consent."

- Evidence liaison: we prefer named contacts in the Order Form (or an appendix) rather than an open procurement inbox. That reduces triage delays. For the Order Form we can add a short table: Redwood evidence liaison / Acme evidence liaison + primary contact and backup.

- Insurance offsets: we can accept language that indemnity obligations are reduced by third‑party insurance proceeds only where such proceeds are actually recovered and applied to the loss. Avoid general offset language that reduces Redwood's liability simply because a policy exists.

If you want, I can prepare two short alternative paragraphs (defend‑control and hybrid) and let Acme pick. That should help move the redline quickly.

Kimberly Park
